findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the silicone sealant between the prep table and wall to be damaged and soiled. The prep table is not bolted in place, and therefore can be moved for cleaning. As long as the table can be pulled from the wall for adequate cleaning, silicone sealant is not required between the table and wall. Ensure the damaged/soiled silicone is removed or replaced prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a wastewater leak from underneath the right basin of the triple sink. A leak or ponding water was not observed at the start of the inspection. The leak seems to have occurred during the inspection. The PIC was notified of the leak and the triple sink was drained. The dish machine in the facility is currently under maintenance, so the triple sink is the facility's sole method of washing and sanitizing. The accommodate their needs, the right basin will be converted to the “rinse” basin with no water held. The facility will wash in the left basin, rinse with running water in the right basin, and sanitize in the center. This is a temporary solution until the sink can be repaired. If the leak worsens and the sink cannot be used at all, the facility has large bins that can be utilized as a temporary triple sink. Staff is educated on preparing temporary washing/sanitizing systems. A follow-up will be conducted on Friday, February 6th to ensure the sink has been repaired.
findings.citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: 3-501.17: Observed container of cheese sauce in cooler to have no date mark. Cheese sauce was discarded during inspection.  (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) CFM was not present in the kitchen. A CFM was on-site but was not overseeing food handling at the time of inspection. Handwashing sinks were not properly stocked, and one handwashing sink was blocked by an upright floor fan (see violation 10 for details). Priority violations were observed for handwashing technique, sanitizer concentration, and hot holding (see violations 8, 21, &, 28 for details). Cook is in the process of completing manager certification and should be done with within the next few weeks. A follow-up inspection will be conducted in 10 days to check on certification and revisit issues observed during the inspection today.  
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Cook was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off prior to obtaining paper towels to dry hands. Proper technique was discussed.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.11 Upon inspector’s arrival, neither of the handwashing sinks were properly stocked. One sink was blocked by a fan and had only soap available. The other handwashing sink had paper towels and no soap. The sink without soap is the location where hands are typically washed, and the cook noted they ran out of soap earlier that morning. It’s not possible to keep hands properly cleaned if sinks are not stocked accordingly. Sinks were provided with supplies. 
Foods employees shall keep their hands and exposed portions of their arms clean.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(1) Five covered aluminum pans of cooked carrots were stacked on the stove top while cook was taking a lunch delivery to the west location. Top two pans of carrots had surface temperatures at 118F (Infant) and 125F (Todder) and internal temperatures at 124F-128F (Infant) and 125F-134F (Toddler) respectively. Surface temperatures for the other three pans stacked below were at 128F-157F, and internal temperatures for the remaining three pans were at 141F-158F. Cook stated pans were temporarily stacked outside of the oven so as not to overcook the carrots. Pans were placed back in the oven (holding at 236F) once cook returned from the delivery, and cook noted this is not a normal practice. Cook was advised to hold cooked foods at 135F/above until it is time for service. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-202.12 Quat solution in spray bottled tested above 400ppm with facility’s test strips and inspector’s test strips. The color that registered on the test strips was not present on the chart. Solution was discarded. A new solution at 200ppm was prepared using half a sani-tab in the spray bottle. Ensure the concentration of solutions prepared with sani-tabs is at 200-400ppm. 
Chemical sanitizers must meet the concentration and use requirements specified by 40 CFR 180.940. Toxics shall be used according to the manufacturer's use directions included in labeling, and must not be used in a manner that poses a health hazard or potential risk of cross contamination.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-401.14 Damp wiping cloth was observed hanging next to the quat spray bottle in the kitchen. Storage of wiping cloths in sanitizer solution between uses was discussed. Wiping cloth was placed in soiled linen bag during inspection.
When using a spray bottle of sanitizer, a wiping cloth may be used one time and then needs to be placed immediately in the soiled linen storage. Otherwise, disposable paper towels should be used with spray bottles of sanitizer. 
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.15 Cook stated mop water is disposed of via the 3 part sink at the end of operations daily. Cook is new within the last few months and is not the person that was present at the last routine inspection. Cook was advised on use of the mop sink (utility closet) and stated they didn’t think a mop sink was available. Inspector showed cook where the mop sink is located and advised of proper disposal of mop water in the designated utility sink. The mop sink needs to be used for the disposal of mop water, and the practice of using the 3 part sink for disposal of mop water needs to stop. Staff agreed to cease using the 3 part sink and begin using the mopsink for disposal of used mop water. Proper disposal of mop water will be revisited on 9/27/21 during follow-up inspection. 
Food preparation sinks, handwashing sinks, and warewashing equipment may not be used for the cleaning of maintenance tools, the preparation or holding of maintenance materials, or the disposal of mop water and similar liquid wastes.

750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) (R) drip tray of stove (food debris/splash);
B) dry storage shelf holding syrup (food splash);   and
C) sprayer - outer surfaces (general buildup).

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.citation_text:
750.1170 - Outer door in kitchen was propped open upon arrival of inspector and does not have a screen door. The door was closed.
Director was advised screening (i.e. screen door, magnetic mesh screening, etc.) of some sort needs to be installed if the door in question is to be propped open. Otherwise, the door may only be propped open during periods when food and other items are being removed from or delivered to the facility (i.e. preparing to deliver lunch to another location, returning dishes from another location, etc.).

Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - Cook was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off prior to drying hands. Proper technique was discussed.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time they may have been contaminated and prior to putting on gloves or working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles. Hands must be lathered for 20 seconds once soap is applied to wet hands. Use paper towels to dry hands and use then the paper towels as a barrier to shut off the manual faucet as the final step of handwashing process..

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - Drip tray of stove was soiled with food debris/splash). Clean the drip tray as needed to eliminate buildup of food debris/splash..

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text:
750.880 - Aluminum pan lids in dry storage were observed to have dried food debris on packaging where product was opened. One lid was outside of the packaging with food surface exposed and some kind of debris on it. Lid outside of packaging was discarded. Discussed storage options for single service items once opened if food debris gets on packaging (remove remaining items and store in plastic bag or in some other manner that protects food contact surfaces).

Single service articles must be stored, handled, and dispensed in a manner that protects against potential contamination.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.citation_text:
750.1390 - Damp mop was stored in the mop bucket. Store mops hanging or inverted to allow for proper drying of wet mop heads.

Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similar equipment shall be maintained and stored properly.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - Open packages of deli meat (turkey) and American cheese slices were not date marked. Products were discarded in the trash.
Open packages of deli ham (just opened today) were dated during inspection (lunch prep was done - product would be kept for use next week)

Properly date mark ready to eat, potentially hazardous foods once packaging is opened and use or discard within 7 days from opening (i.e. opened 9/18 = use or discard by the end of the day on 9/24). Date must also be marked on open containers of milk, soy milk, and almond milk, even if it is a product for an individual child brought in by parents.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Plastic storage tub with red and blue tongs stored inside had food debris and mold growth inside. Tub and tongs were set aside at 3 part sink to go through ware washing process.

Food and food contact surfaces must be protected from cross contamination at all times. **Mold growth in a covered container means that spores and toxins are present in the container and may potentially contaminate the surfaces of tongs. Clean and sanitize utensils storage containers frequently and maintain clean.**

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Cook was observed slicing oranges straight from the original cardboard box in which they were received. Cooked was asked about cleaning process prior to prep; cook noted he rinses all of the oranges upon delivery. Cook and Owner were advised the original box is not considered a clean surfaces. Once the oranges are rinsed they need to be stored in a clean, food grade container or the box must be lined with a food safe liner if oranges are rinsed upon delivery and then stored. Otherwise, rinse oranges as needed prior to slicing.

Food shall be properly stored and protected at all times. **Once produce is rinsed, especially produce that will be sliced and knife will be touching outer peel and inner fruit, the food needs to be stored in a manner that will protect the outer surface of the product from potential contamination prior to slicing.**

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) can opener blade (debris);
B) ceiling inside microwave (dried splash);   and
C) hood baffles (dust).

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris. In-use equipment must be cleaned and sanitized up to every 4hrs after continuous use (i.e. can opener, etc.).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - Drip tray of stove was soiled with accumulation of food/splash. Clean the drip tray as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1200 & 1220 - A) Divider between 3 part sink and clean dish shelving:
1. (R) Gap was present along the floor to wall juncture of the divider on the 3 part sink side by the corner.
2. (R) Baseboard was loose at the front corner on the clean dish shelving side. Debris accumulation was noted in the area. 
3. Section of metal was screwed at the floor to wall juncture of the divider on the 3 part sink side adjacent to the area where the gap was present.
Remove the  screws from the floor to wall juncture (not conducive to easy cleaning). Re-seal the floor to wall juncture on the 3 part sink side of the divider. Re-attach the front corner of the baseboard on the clean dish side of the divider or remove baseboard and seal floor to wall juncture with silicone or caulk.

B) Flooring:
1. (R) Floor covering around floor drain by dish machine was loose. Re-seal the covering to the tiles around the floor drain.
2. (R) Floor covering was separating at the seam between the dish machine and prep table. Seal the gap at the seams of the floor covering.

Floors must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean. Junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.  (see general comments)

findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
findings.comment: See 4/28/15 report for details

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: See 4/28/15 report for details

findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
findings.citation_text:
750.830 - Dish machine was leaking water out the front along the sides of the door seal during ware washing cycles. Staff noted this is a new issue that just started since the weather warmed up recently. Call for maintenance and get the machine check/repaired. The water leaking around the door seal is more than likely contributing to the issue with water damaged floor tiles (see #36). 

Dish machines shall be properly installed and maintained in good repair. Dish machines shall be operated in accordance with the manufacturers instructions.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Wet wiping cloth was hanging on the sanitizer bucket and only a portion of the cloth was submerged in sanitizer solution. Wiping cloth was completely submerged in solution by inspector.

Store wet wiping cloths completely submerged in sanitizer solution between uses to inhibit the growth of microorganisms. Maintain quat solution at 200-400ppm. Change solutions every 2 to 4 hours or more frequently if solutions and wiping cloths become heavily soiled.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - Can opener blade and holder were soiled with debris buildup. Clean and sanitize the can opener and holder between uses/as needed.

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed, up to every 4hrs after continuous use, to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) floor fan in dry storage (dust); 
B) wall mounted chemical storage rack under 3 part sink (debris);   and
C) top of in-use rinse aid container under 3 part sink (moisture/debris).

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.citation_text:
750.1120 - Handsink near back door was blocked by lunch materials/supplies awaiting delivery to the other facilities. Items were on the floor surrounding the radius around the handsink. All items were removed from the area over time. 
 
Handsinks are to accessible for handwashing at all times. Always maintain a clear path to both handsinks to allow for proper handwashing. Establish a storage system that does not impede the use of handsinks during prep/prior to delivery.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.citation_text:
750.1160 - Ants were observed along the floor to wall juncture of the divider between the 3 part sink and clean dish shelving and on the wall around/behind the dish machine and 3 part sink. A couple ants were also observed on a piece of food debris under the clean dish shelving. Clean, minimize the presence of water, and make necessary repairs in the dish area (see #36 for details on repairs needed). Call pest control operator for service.

Effective measures to minimize the presence of pests shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1200 & 1220 - A) Divider between 3 part sink and clean dish shelving:
1. Gap was present along the floor to wall juncture of the divider on the 3 part sink side by the corner. Water was observed on the floor, and puddling water was noted in the area where the gap was present. 
2. Baseboard was loose at the front corner on the clean dish shelving side. Debris accumulation was noted in the area. 
Clean and eliminate puddling water from the aforementioned areas. Re-seal the floor to wall juncture on all sides of the divider. 

B) Flooring:
1. Floor covering under/around dish machine was loose and had water damage in several areas. Water accumulation was present in some areas. 
2. Floor covering was separating at the seam between the dish machine and the prep table.
Flooring must be removed and replaced in areas where water damage has occurred. Otherwise, attempts may be made to re-seal around where seams are pulling apart.

C) Food and general debris were observed behind/under the dish machine.
Clean under/behind the dish machine.

Floors must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean. Junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.  (see general comments)

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - Can opener blade was soiled with debris buildup. Can opener was cleaned/sanitized in the dish machine.

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed, up to every 4hrs after continuous use, to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text:
750.860 - A) Storage containers for clean measuring cups and utensils were starting to accumulate crumbs/debris in the bottom.
Clean and sanitize storage containers for utensils and other equipment as needed and maintain them clean.

B) Food tongs were observed with food surfaces extended up out of measuring cup used for storage.
Store utensils with handles extended out to protect food contact surfaces from contamination during storage and retrieval.
 
Cleaned and sanitized utensils/equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text:
750.120 & 130 - Container of grapes was observed on the floor with various items awaiting delivery to another location. Grapes were elevated off the floor and placed on top of other containers of grapes that were not on the floor. Proper food storage was discussed with cook and owner. 
Food shall be protected at all times.  Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.citation_text:
750.1120 - Handsinks were not easily accessible upon arrival of inspector. One handsink was blocked with a bowl sitting in the basin. The other handsink was difficult to reach because various items were stacked on floor in front of the sink awaiting delivery to another location. The bowl was removed from the basin of the one handsink. Items on the floor in front of the other handsink were repositioned to allow for easier access.
Handsinks shall be accessible to employees at all times. Do not store anything in the basins of handsinks. A clear path should always be present to allow for ease in access and proper handwashing at all times during food prep/service.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.citation_text:
750.1300 - Spray bottle of pink colored liquid was not labeled as to the contents. Test strip was used to verify it was quat sanitizer (200ppm). Owner labeled the spray bottle during the inspection. Maintain proper labels on all chemical bottles.
Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.citation_text: 750.1120 - Handsink was used to rinse a container of strawberries. Cook and Owner were advised on proper use of handsinks and proper handwashing technique. Handsinks are to be used for handwashing only and must always be accessible for handwashing. The only time a handsink should be unaccessible would be when it is in use for handwashing by another individual. If other tasks besides handwashing are conducted at a handsink it is considered blocked regardless of how quickly the tasks occur. Properly use handsinks, and use the 3 part sink for all other tasks in the kitchen (clean and sanitize 3 part sink basins before and after use/between tasks).

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.citation_text: 750.1170 - Bottom right side of the blue door frame in the kitchen was rusted out in a few spots both inside and outside of the door. Daylight was visible. Owner used steel wool and caulk as a temporary fix to seal the area and eliminate a potential entry point for pests. Owner stated the door frame will probably need to be replaced, which can be a costly venture/may not occur right away. The temporary fix of steel wool/caulk will suffice until permanent repairs can be made and/or the door frame is replaced as long as the temporary fix is maintained to provide a tight fitting, vermin proof seal. Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.citation_text: 750.100 - Can of tomato sauce with a severe dent in the bottom seam was opened to make spaghetti sauce. Can was placed by the back door to be discarded, and a new can that was in good condition was opened for use. Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption. Cans must never be used if they are dented on the top, bottom, or side seams or if cans have any other kind of severe damage. (see general comments)

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 750.160, 510, 512, 530 - (x2) Employee was observed with personal drink in prep area. The personal drink was discarded. He then continued working with the same pair of gloves. When asked to remove gloves and wash his hands, proper handwashing technique was not used (did not apply soap to hands). Proper handwashing and glove use were discussed. Employee began changing gloves and washing hands as needed. Change gloves between tasks/as needed. Hands must be properly washed before putting on gloves, between glove changes, any time hands may have become contaminated, and prior to handling food or clean equipment. Only eat/drink in designated areas separate from food prep/storage. **Educational handouts on handwashing and single use gloves were provided**

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text: 750.810 - Wiping cloth used for general surfaces was sitting in 3 part sink. No sanitizer solution was setup for general surfaces. Wet wiping cloth was taken to laundry room. Spray bottle of bleach water was made at 100ppm. Use paper towels when spray bottles of sanitizer are in use and discard the paper towels after one time use. If wiping cloths are used, a bucket of sanitizer solution must be maintained so wiping cloths may be placed in the solution between uses. Maintain sanitizer solution for general surfaces in the kitchen at all times of prep/operation.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed American cheese stored in the 2 dr cooler(upright) to not be labeled or dated. Label and date all food that is left opened in cooler.
750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Single service articles not re-used
findings.comment:
Observed a container that had blueberry yogurt in it--to have ketchup in it now. Do not reuse single service containers. Provide another container or ziplock bags for left over or small portion.
750-600 Re-use of single-service articles is prohibited. Do not re-use single service items.

findings.title: Containers covered, adequate number, insect and rodent proof, emptied at proper intervals, clean
findings.comment:
Observed the dumpsters outside to have an open door on both. Close the lids to garbage dumpster.
750-1130a Garbage and refuse shall be kept in durable easily cleanable, insect-proof, and rodent-proof containers.
